about: About these leads

Leaflegal sends trademark and IP enquiries from businesses and individuals across the UK who want to pay a professional to protect or defend a brand, creative work or product design. They come from business owners preparing to launch, growing brands, online sellers, product businesses, agencies and creators. Each enquiry goes to one firm only. It is never sent to several firms at once and it is never resold after delivery.

Trademark clients usually come to us at a clear decision point. Some are about to spend money on a name and want to know it is safe. Some have received an examination report, a notice of opposition or a letter from a competitor and are working to a fixed deadline. Others have found copies of their products online and want them taken down. These are people who already know they need help and are ready to talk about it.

Because there is one UK trademark register, enquiries can come from England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland. You choose the matter types you want and whether you take enquiries from anywhere in the UK or only certain regions.

We introduce trademark enquiries to solicitors regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority and to chartered trade mark attorneys regulated by IPReg. Both are well placed to handle searches, filings and UK IPO proceedings. Where a matter is likely to need court action, firms that can litigate, or that work with litigators, are often the best fit, and you can tell us which matter types you want.

Our campaigns run on search, social media and helpful content aimed at the moments people need trademark help, such as searching for how to trademark a name, how to oppose a trademark or what to do about a cease and desist letter. Each person answers a short set of questions about what they want to protect, what they need, whether they have filed already, any deadline and the size of the business. When an enquiry matches your settings, we send it to you as soon as it has been checked.

Leaflegal is not a law firm and does not give legal advice. We do not tell clients whether their mark is registrable, whether they infringe or what classes they need. We introduce them to one firm that handles trademark work, and the advice comes from you.

about.h3: Why trademark work suits exclusive leads

about: Trademark clients are often at the start of a long relationship with their adviser. A business that files its first mark today may need logos, new product names, international filings, watching, renewals and the occasional dispute over the years that follow. When an enquiry goes to several firms at once, the client tends to choose on price alone. When it goes to one firm, you have the space to explain your approach, build trust and win the relationship as well as the first instruction.

Many trademark enquiries also arrive with a deadline. An examination report, an opposition window or a reply date in a cease and desist letter gives the client a reason to act now rather than later. Exclusive introductions mean you are not racing other firms to the phone while the client is trying to meet that deadline.
Who enquires

Trademark enquiries come from a broad mix of clients. Many are small and medium sized businesses without an in house legal team, which makes them a good fit for firms that offer clear fixed fees and practical advice.

about.h3: Where they are in the process

about: Some clients are at the idea stage with a shortlist of names. Others have filed themselves and hit an objection. Some have a registered mark and a problem with a copier, and some are on the receiving end of a complaint. The form records which, so you know before you call whether you are talking about a filing, a deadline or a dispute.

Most trademark clients want to understand quickly whether they have a problem, what it will cost to deal with and how long it will take. Clear fixed fees for searches and filings, a plain explanation of official fees and a realistic view of disputes go a long way. Many become long term portfolio clients if the first matter goes well.

Most clients don't use technical language. They say things like someone has copied my brand on Amazon, I got a letter saying my name is too similar, or I want to protect my logo. The form turns that into a matter type and a set of tags, and the description in their own words often adds useful colour about the business and what is at stake. It is worth reading before you call.

Not every client is a company. Photographers, illustrators, writers and musicians enquire about copied work, and individuals sometimes receive image claims for personal or side business websites. These matters are often smaller but quick to resolve, and you can choose whether you want them.
Lead details
Every lead includes the full set of answers the client gave, in the order they gave them, along with checked contact details and a record of the consent they gave to be contacted by a firm.

about: Answers carry short tags, such as international, pending application, defend opposition, marketplace, portfolio or high value, so we can match leads to the work you want. If you only want filings and searches, or only disputes, tell us and we will set your filters accordingly.

People who want patent advice, free advice only or who are just researching are shown helpful resources before they submit and never become leads. That keeps your leads focused on clients with a real matter and a willingness to pay.

Where the client gives a date, such as the deadline on an examination report, the end of an opposition period, a reply date in a letter or a renewal expiry, it is sent as the lead's deadline. That makes it easy to triage leads that need same day attention.

The lead also records the exact wording of each question and answer, so you can see precisely what the client was asked. That helps avoid misunderstandings, for example about whether they have already filed or whether a letter they received came from a solicitor or the brand owner directly.
Working the lead
Trademark enquiries reward speed and clarity. A client with a deadline wants to know someone is on it. A client with a new brand wants a clear plan and a price.

Call as soon as you can, ideally within the hour. Confirm what the client told us, ask any follow up questions and explain what happens next. Many firms send a short written summary and fee quote the same day.

list: Can you send me the mark and a link to how you use it?
What exactly do you sell, and what do you plan to sell next?
Have you searched or filed anything already?
Is there a date on any letter or notice you have received?
Where do you trade, and is international protection on the horizon?

about.h3: Turning one matter into a relationship

about: A client who registers one mark often needs more as they grow, such as logos, new product names, international filings, watching and renewals. A client who wins a dispute with your help is likely to come back. Exclusive introductions give you a fair chance to build that relationship without competing with several other firms on the first call.
Where a lead mentions a deadline, such as an opposition period or a reply date, prioritise it. If you can't help in time, tell the client quickly so they can look elsewhere, and let us know.

Trademark clients are often surprised that there are two sets of fees, the official UK IPO fees and the professional fees. A short, clear explanation on the first call, followed by a written quote that separates the two, builds confidence and avoids misunderstandings later. Fixed fees for common work, such as searches, filings and simple replies to examination reports, tend to convert well.

about.h3: When the matter isn't a fit

about: If an enquiry turns out to need work you don't do, such as a patent or a court claim outside your jurisdiction, tell the client promptly and, if you can, point them to someone who can help. Let us know too, so we can adjust your settings. Our invalid lead rules cover enquiries that fall outside the settings you agreed.

Not every client instructs on the first call. Some need to talk to a business partner, a designer or an investor first. A short follow up a few days later, with a reminder of any deadline and a clear next step, often makes the difference. Keep notes of what the client told you so the follow up feels personal.
Compliance
Leaflegal is built to fit the professional rules that apply to solicitors and trade mark attorneys.

SRA regulated firms must tell clients in writing about any referral fee paid for an introduction, and the fee must not affect the client's interests or the firm's independence. IPReg regulated attorneys must also act in their clients' best interests and be open with them about relevant arrangements. Every client is told before they submit that Leaflegal is paid by the firms it introduces, and we ask firms to confirm the fee in their client care letter.

Each client ticks a separate box agreeing to be contacted by one firm about their matter. The consent wording and the time it was given are recorded and sent with the lead. We share only what is needed for you to contact the client about the matter they raised.
Our pages and form give general information only. We don't tell clients whether their mark can be registered, whether they infringe or what to do. That keeps the advice where it belongs, with you.

You remain responsible for conflict checks, client identification and your own regulatory obligations. Some trademark matters, such as disputes, can raise conflicts with existing clients, so check before taking instructions.

Our campaigns and pages describe the service accurately, make clear that Leaflegal is an introducer and not a law firm, and avoid promising outcomes. We don't use your firm's name in our advertising without your agreement.
If you have questions about how the introduction works in practice, such as what clients are told and when, we are happy to walk through the form and the consent wording on your onboarding call.
Pricing

You pay per lead, at a price agreed with you before you start. Pricing depends on the matter types and locations you choose. There is a minimum of 10 leads a month, and you set a monthly cap. You can pause at any time.

Your written agreement covers pricing, billing, how leads are delivered and our rules for invalid leads, such as wrong contact details or matters outside your settings. Leads are delivered by email or straight into your CRM or case management system as soon as they have been checked.

Start with a 30 minute call with our team. We will talk through the matter types you want, whether you take enquiries from across the UK, likely volumes and pricing, and show you a sample lead before you commit to anything.

Trademark solicitors, IP teams within commercial firms and chartered trade mark attorney firms that handle UK filings and brand disputes. Firms that offer fixed fees for searches and filings and can respond quickly to deadline driven matters tend to do best. You must be authorised and competent for the work you take on.

Pricing reflects the value and type of matter. Dispute and deadline driven matters are often priced differently from straightforward filings and searches. We will talk through the options on your call and agree a price for each matter type you choose.
Before you commit, we will explain how the minimum works, how invalid leads are handled and how billing runs, so there are no surprises once leads start arriving.
faqs: The leads
What are trademark leads?

They are enquiries from people and businesses who want to pay a professional to help with a trademark or related IP matter, such as a filing, a search, an opposition, a dispute, a renewal, copyright or design rights. Each completed our own enquiry form about their own matter and asked to be contacted.
Are trademark leads exclusive?
Yes. Each enquiry goes to one firm only and is never resold. The client hears from you and no other firm through Leaflegal.
Do you send patent enquiries?
No. Patent enquiries are turned away before submission and directed to patent attorney resources. Our IP leads cover trademarks, copyright and design rights only.
Can I take only filings and searches?

Yes. You choose the matter types you want. Many attorney firms take filings, searches and oppositions but not court disputes, and some litigation teams want only infringement and cease and desist matters.
Do leads include copyright claims?
Yes, if you choose them. Copyright leads include businesses that have received image claims and creators whose work has been copied, as well as contract and ownership questions.
How do you know the client is serious?

Each client confirms they are ready to pay for help, gives a verified mobile and email and ticks a separate consent box. People who are only researching or want free advice are shown resources instead of submitting.
Do leads include business size?
Business clients are asked for a turnover band, and many give one. Some prefer not to say. Company clients can also be matched to their Companies House record.
Do leads include international filing enquiries?
Yes. Clients who plan to trade abroad are tagged international, so firms that handle Madrid and overseas filings can choose them. Many clients start with the UK and add other countries later.
Do you send enquiries from people who have already filed themselves?
Yes. Many clients file without help and then enquire when they receive an objection or an opposition. The lead tells you the stage reached so you can prepare.
Do leads say who sent a letter the client received?

The client tells us what they have received, such as a letter from a solicitor or a brand owner, a marketplace takedown or a court claim. They often add detail in their own words. You can confirm the rest on the first call.
Do trademark leads convert well?

It depends on how quickly and clearly the firm follows up. We don't publish conversion figures. Firms that call promptly, explain official and professional fees simply and offer fixed fees for common work tend to do best.
Volume and areas
Do trademark leads come from across the UK?
Yes. Because there is one UK register, trademark enquiries can come from England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland. You can take national enquiries or limit them to certain regions.
How many trademark leads can I expect?
Volumes depend on the matter types and regions you choose and on demand at the time. We will give you an honest view on your call before you commit. We never promise volumes we can't deliver.
Can I set a monthly cap?
Yes. You set your monthly volume, with a minimum of 10 leads a month, and you can pause at any time.
Do you work with attorney firms as well as solicitors?
Yes. We work with chartered trade mark attorneys regulated by IPReg and with solicitors regulated by the SRA.
What if I can only act in England and Wales for court work?
Tell us. We can limit dispute matters to England and Wales while sending filings and searches from across the UK.
Can I receive leads for just one matter type?
Yes, as long as the volume makes sense for both of us. Some firms only want oppositions or only want infringement matters. We will give you an honest view of likely volumes on your call.
Are some months busier than others?
Demand varies with business launches, marketplace activity and seasonal trading, and with how our campaigns are performing. We will discuss what to expect on your call and keep you updated.
Compliance
Are referral fees allowed for trademark work?

Paying for introductions is permitted for trademark work, which is not covered by the personal injury referral fee ban. SRA firms must tell clients about the fee in writing, and IPReg attorneys must act in clients' best interests and be transparent. We tell every client before they submit that firms pay us.
What consent do you record?
Each client ticks a separate box agreeing to be contacted by one firm about their matter. We record the wording and the time and send them with the lead.
Do you give clients advice?
No. Leaflegal gives general information only. All advice comes from the firm we introduce.
Who is responsible for conflict checks?
You are. Trademark disputes can involve businesses you already act for, so please run your usual checks before taking instructions.
How is client data handled?
We share only the information needed to contact the client about their matter, and only with the one firm we introduce. Our agreement with you covers data protection responsibilities.
Do clients know they are being introduced to one firm?
Yes. The form and our pages explain that we pass each enquiry to one firm that handles that kind of matter, and that the firm pays us for the introduction.
Pricing and terms
How much do trademark leads cost?
Pay per lead, at a price agreed with you before you start. The price depends on the matter types and locations you choose. We don't publish a price list because it varies with your settings.
Is there a minimum?
Yes, the minimum is 10 leads a month. Above that, you set your volume and can pause at any time.
What happens if a lead is invalid?
Your written agreement sets out our invalid lead rules, for example wrong contact details or matters outside your settings. Leads that qualify under those rules are replaced or credited.
How are leads delivered?
By email or straight into your CRM or case management system, as soon as they have been checked.
Is there a contract?
Yes. A written agreement covers pricing, billing, delivery and invalid lead rules, so both sides know exactly how it works.
Do I pay for leads I don't take on?

You pay for leads that match your settings, whether or not the client instructs you. Leads that fall under the invalid lead rules in your agreement are replaced or credited. Converting leads is part of the work, and we are happy to share what tends to work well.
Can I change my settings later?
Yes. You can change matter types, regions and your monthly volume by letting us know. Changes usually take effect quickly.
Getting started
How do I start receiving trademark leads?
Book a 30 minute call with our team. We will discuss the matter types and regions you want, likely volumes and pricing, and show you a sample lead before you commit.
Can I see a sample lead?
Yes. We show you a sample on your call, so you can see exactly what you will receive.
How quickly can I start?
Once your settings and agreement are in place, leads can start flowing as soon as matching enquiries come in. We will agree a start date on your call.
Can I add other practice areas later?
Yes. If your firm also handles commercial work such as debt recovery or licensing, you can add those areas at any time.
Is there an online platform?
Leads are delivered by email or into your own systems. Talk to us on your call about how you would like to receive them.
What do you need from us to set up?
Your matter types, regions, monthly volume, delivery details and who should receive leads, plus your regulator and registration details. We cover all of this on the onboarding call.
Can we talk before committing?
Yes. The onboarding call is a conversation, not a sales commitment. If the service isn't a good fit for your firm, we will tell you honestly.
